text:
[on-screen: STOP WRITING PROMPTS]
Stop writing your own prompts.
You're likely the bottleneck in your agent's performance.

[on-screen: THE META-LAYER]
I spent weeks hand-tuning a complex logic chain for a production system.
It was fine.
Then I built a meta-layer to let the agent optimize its own instructions based on success metrics.

[on-screen: THE RESULT]
The output was strange.
It used structural anchors and specific token weights I would've never considered.
It stripped away the polite prose I thought was helping.
The performance jumped by twenty percent.

[on-screen: PROMPT VS MAP]
Engineers treat prompts like human conversation.
Models treat them like high-dimensional coordinate maps.
A self-improving system finds paths through that latent space that human intuition can't see.
Stop trying to be a prompt engineer.
Start being an AI architect who builds self-evolving systems.

[on-screen: TOOLS VS STRINGS]
Are you still hand-tuning strings or are you building the logic that tunes them for you.

#AIEngineering #LLMOps #AIArchitecture
idea_source: How I built a self-improving AI agent that evolves its own prompts
